# (PART) Continental Ternary Partitioning & Figures {-}

# Continental Application & Dominance Regimes (`apply_model7()`) {#application}

```{r ch8-setup, include = FALSE}
source('R/00_setup.R')
```

## Continental 3-LAC Application Dataset (`n = 478,929`)

Because the calibrated bio-optical model requires only the three constituent concentrations ($\text{NAP}$, $\text{DOC}$, and $\text{Chl }a$) to partition non-water light attenuation, Model 7 can be applied to every simultaneous 3-LAC sample in the harmonized AquaMatch dataset—with or without a paired Secchi depth measurement—provided that:

1. $\text{Chl }a$, $\text{DOC}$, and $\text{TSS}$ were measured synchronously at a non-facility monitoring station (with sub-detection entries floored at the standard analytical reporting limits of `Section 4`);
2. Each constituent (and Secchi depth, if measured) lies within the empirical range of the training dataset (`Section 4`) so the regression model is never extrapolated beyond its calibration domain; and
3. $\text{NAP} > `r P$apply_min_nap`\text{ mg L}^{-1}$ so all three constituent concentrations are strictly positive.

```{r application}
app <- get_application(); tr <- get_training()
tibble(set = c('4-Variable Training Dataset (Secchi + 3 LACs measured, screened)',
               'Continental 3-LAC Application Dataset (within training bounds & NAP > 0.01 mg/L)',
               '  ├── Application records with Measured Secchi depth',
               '  └── Application records with Modeled Secchi depth only (no measured Secchi)'),
       n = c(nrow(tr), nrow(app), sum(!is.na(app$secchi)), sum(is.na(app$secchi))),
       sites = c(n_distinct(tr$SiteID), n_distinct(app$SiteID),
                 n_distinct(app$SiteID[!is.na(app$secchi)]), n_distinct(app$SiteID[is.na(app$secchi)]))) %>%
  mutate(across(c(n, sites), fmt_n)) %>%
  kable(col.names = c('Dataset Subset', 'Observations (n)', 'Unique Monitoring Sites')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = FALSE)
```

## Ternary Attenuation Fractions & Secchi Prediction

For each observation $r$ assigned specific attenuation coefficients $(\alpha_{\text{NAP}}, \alpha_{\text{DOC}}, \alpha_{\text{Chl }a})$ from its Level III ecoregion in Model 7 (or global Model 1 fallback if the ecoregion has $\le 100$ observations or a non-positive slope estimate):

$$f_{i,r} = \frac{\alpha_i C_{i,r}}{\alpha_{\text{NAP}}\,\text{NAP}_r + \alpha_{\text{DOC}}\,\text{DOC}_r + \alpha_{\text{Chl }a}\,\text{Chl }a_r}, \qquad i \in \{\text{NAP}, \text{DOC}, \text{Chl }a\}, \qquad \sum_{i} f_{i,r} = 1$$

and total diffuse attenuation and Secchi depth are predicted using the **consistent** training pure-water offset $k_w = `r round(get_k_w(), 5)`\text{ m}^{-1}$:

$$\hat{k}_{d,r} = k_w + \alpha_{\text{NAP}}\,\text{NAP}_r + \alpha_{\text{DOC}}\,\text{DOC}_r + \alpha_{\text{Chl }a}\,\text{Chl }a_r, \qquad \hat{z}_{SD,r} = \frac{1}{\hat{k}_{d,r}}$$

```{r final-data}
fd <- get_final_data()
fd %>% count(type, model) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = n) %>%
  mutate(Total = z3 + global,
         `% Model 7 (Level III)` = sprintf('%.1f%%', 100 * z3 / Total)) %>%
  rename(`Water-Body Type` = type,
         `Model 7 (Level III Ecoregion)` = z3,
         `Model 1 (Global Fallback)` = global) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), fmt_n)) %>%
  kable() %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = FALSE)
```

Across all **`r fmt_n(nrow(fd))`** application observations, **`r round(100 * mean(fd$model == 'z3'), 1)`%** (`r fmt_n(sum(fd$model == 'z3'))` records) use Level III ecoregion-specific Model 7 coefficients and **`r round(100 * mean(fd$model == 'global'), 1)`%** (`r fmt_n(sum(fd$model == 'global'))` records) use the global Model 1 fallback, with **zero observations** falling outside the $[0, 1]^3$ ternary simplex.

## Continental Mean Ternary Partitioning by Water-Body Type {#intext}

```{r means}
bind_rows(fd %>% mutate(type = 'All Waters'), fd) %>%
  mutate(type = factor(type, c('All Waters', 'Stream', 'Lake', 'Estuary'))) %>%
  group_by(type) %>%
  summarize(n = n(), sites = n_distinct(SiteID),
             DOC = mean(doc_kd), NAP = mean(tss_kd), `Chl a` = mean(chl_kd),
             sd_DOC = sd(doc_kd), sd_NAP = sd(tss_kd), `sd_Chl a` = sd(chl_kd)) %>%
  mutate(across(c(DOC:`sd_Chl a`), ~ percent(.x, 0.1)),
         n = fmt_n(n), sites = fmt_n(sites)) %>%
  kable(col.names = c('Water-Body Type', 'Observations (n)', 'Unique Sites', 'Mean DOC %', 'Mean NAP %', 'Mean Chl a %', 'SD DOC', 'SD NAP', 'SD Chl a'),
        caption = 'Arithmetic mean and standard deviation of non-water light-attenuation fractions across the continental dataset (blue centroids in Figure 2).') %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = TRUE)
```

Across all **`r fmt_n(nrow(fd))`** observations, mean non-water light attenuation is dominated by **DOC (`r percent(mean(fd$doc_kd), 0.1)`)**, followed by **NAP (`r percent(mean(fd$tss_kd), 0.1)`)** and **Chl *a* (`r percent(mean(fd$chl_kd), 0.1)`)**. Streams (`56.0% DOC, 37.3% NAP, 6.7% Chl a`) and estuaries (`55.5% DOC, 38.7% NAP, 5.8% Chl a`) share similar optical partitioning along the DOC–NAP axis, whereas lakes (`58.1% DOC, 25.2% NAP, 16.6% Chl a`) exhibit more than double the mean phytoplankton attenuation share and substantially broader dispersion across ternary space (`Figure 2c`).

## Hypothesis Tests of Water Clarity Across $>80\%$ Dominance Classes ($p < 0.01$) {#dominance-test}

To evaluate how absolute water clarity ($z_{SD}$) varies with optical regime, observations are classified into four dominance classes based on whether a single constituent accounts for $> 80\%$ of non-water light attenuation (`P$dominance_threshold = 0.80`): **NAP-dominant** ($f_{\text{NAP}} > 0.80$), **Chl *a*-dominant** ($f_{\text{Chl }a} > 0.80$), **DOC-dominant** ($f_{\text{DOC}} > 0.80$), and **Mixed** (no single constituent $> 0.80$).

```{r secchi-classes}
dom <- test_dominance_secchi(fd)
dom$summary %>%
  transmute(
    `Dominance Regime (>80%)` = class,
    `Observations (n)` = fmt_n(n_obs),
    `Unique Sites` = fmt_n(n_sites),
    `Mean Modeled Secchi (m)` = round(mean_secchi_pred, 2),
    `SD (m)` = round(sd_secchi_pred, 2),
    `SE (m)` = round(se_secchi_pred, 4),
    `Median Modeled Secchi (m)` = round(median_secchi_pred, 2),
    `Mean Combined Secchi (m)` = round(mean_secchi_combined, 2),
    `Mean Measured Secchi (m)` = round(mean_secchi_measured, 2)
  ) %>%
  kable(caption = 'Secchi disk depth summary statistics across the four >80% constituent dominance regimes.') %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = TRUE)
```

```{r secchi-omnibus}
dom$omnibus %>%
  mutate(p_value = format.pval(p_value, digits = 3, eps = 1e-300)) %>%
  kable(col.names = c('Omnibus Test Across 4 Dominance Regimes', 'Test Statistic', 'p-value')) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = 'condensed')
```

```{r secchi-pairwise}
dom$pairwise %>%
  transmute(
    `Pairwise Comparison` = Comparison,
    `Mean Difference (m)` = round(diff_m, 3),
    `Welch t-test p (Holm-adj.)` = format.pval(p_welch_holm, digits = 3, eps = 1e-300),
    `Wilcoxon rank-sum p (Holm-adj.)` = format.pval(p_wilcoxon_holm, digits = 3, eps = 1e-300),
    `Significant at p < 0.01?` = ifelse(pass_p01_welch & pass_p01_wilcoxon, '✔ Yes (p < 0.01)', 'No')
  ) %>%
  kable(caption = 'All 6 pairwise Secchi depth comparisons across the four dominance regimes.') %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = TRUE)
```

::: {.decision}
**Reconciling Frequency of DOC Dominance with Magnitude of NAP Turbidity**

1. **Frequency vs. intensity of attenuation.** Across the continental dataset, **DOC** is the most *frequent* primary attenuator (`116,567` DOC-dominant samples with mean $z_{SD} = 1.10\text{ m}$, because even clear headwater streams and oligotrophic lakes contain background humic DOC when suspended sediment and algal concentrations are low). In contrast, when **NAP** exceeds 80% of non-water attenuation (`25,793` samples, typically during storm-flow sediment pulses or in erosive rivers), total suspended mass concentrations are high, yielding the **lowest absolute water clarity** (mean $z_{SD} = 0.40\text{ m}$, median $0.24\text{ m}$), followed by hyper-eutrophic **Chl *a*-dominant** blooms (mean $z_{SD} = 0.71\text{ m}$, median $0.38\text{ m}$), **DOC-dominant** waters ($1.10\text{ m}$), and **Mixed** waters ($1.23\text{ m}$).
2. **All 6 pairwise differences satisfy $p < 0.01$.** Under both Holm-adjusted Welch heteroscedastic $t$-tests ($\max p = 1.49 \times 10^{-4}$), non-parametric Wilcoxon rank-sum tests ($\max p = 3.27 \times 10^{-7}$), and equal-variance Tukey HSD tests ($\max p = 0.0042$), all six pairwise comparisons are highly significant ($p < 0.01$).
:::
